sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सत्यम् च ज्ञानम् च आनन्दः च सत्यज्ञानानन्दाः; सत्यज्ञानानन्दाः रूपम् यस्याः सा सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: satyam ca jñānam ca ānandaḥ ca satyajñānānandāḥ; satyajñānānandāḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā satyajñānānandarūpā
samasa.explanation: (1) satya-jñāna-ānanda 'truth, knowledge and bliss' is a dvandva of three equal members. (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose form (rūpa) is truth, knowledge and bliss'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā to agree with Her. The three are not three qualities She possesses but Her very nature, which is why rūpa is used.

components.note: rūpa 'form', with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is truth, knowledge and bliss
names.significance: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad defines Brahman as satyaṃ jñānam anantam and teaches that bliss (ānanda) is Brahman; the name gives the Goddess the Vedāntic svarūpa-lakṣaṇa, sat-cit-ānanda.
names.previous_split_issues: jñānānanda was left as one row; it is jñāna + ānanda, fused by savarṇa-dīrgha.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound parāyaṇa; the n of ayana then becomes ṇ after the r (ṇatva)

samasa.vigraha: परम् अयनम् परायणम्; सामरस्यम् परायणम् यस्याः सा सामरस्यपरायणा
samasa.vigraha_iast: param ayanam parāyaṇam; sāmarasyam parāyaṇam yasyāḥ sā sāmarasyaparāyaṇā
samasa.explanation: (1) para-ayana 'the highest resort, final goal' (karmadhāraya; as a lexical word, 'wholly devoted to'). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose highest resort is sāmarasya', i.e. who is wholly intent on it. Sāmarasya, 'the state of having one flavor', is an abstract noun from sama-rasa 'of equal flavor'.

components.note: abstract noun from samarasa 'of the same flavor' (sama + rasa), with vṛddhi of the first vowel
ayana from √i 'to go'; feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi; ayana → -āyaṇa in the compound

names.meaning: She who is wholly intent on sāmarasya, the perfect equipoise of Śiva and Śakti
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā and Kashmir Śaivism sāmarasya is the 'single flavor' of Śiva and Śakti in union, where consciousness and its power are tasted as one; the Goddess abides in that state and leads the devotee into it.

meaning_check.note: 'Steady wisdom' does not translate sāmarasya, the technical term for the union in one flavor of Śiva and Śakti (or of the individual and the Supreme).

names.previous_split_issues: sāmarasya was glossed 'equality/harmony' without its technical sense; parāyaṇā is para + ayana, not a single unanalysed word.

components.meaning: consort of Kapardin; also, wearing braided locks
components.note: kaparda 'braided, matted hair' + the possessive suffix -in gives kapardin, an epithet of Śiva; feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is the consort of Kapardin, Śiva of the matted locks
names.significance: Śiva is Kapardin, 'the one with the braided coil of hair'; as His inseparable power She bears the same name in the feminine. The feminine can also describe Her own braided hair.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS-style spelling and 'kapardi' tidied to Kapardin; meaning otherwise kept.

names.uncertain: The feminine of kapardin can mean 'wife of Kapardin' (the usual reading) or 'She who herself wears the kaparda braid'.

samasa.vigraha: कलानाम् माला कलामाला; अथवा कलाः माला यस्याः सा कलामाला
samasa.vigraha_iast: kalānām mālā kalāmālā; athavā kalāḥ mālā yasyāḥ sā kalāmālā
samasa.explanation: As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa mālā 'garland' is the head: 'the garland of the arts', She herself being that garland. As a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose garland is the arts', i.e. who wears them. Both readings are current; the second matches the traditional paraphrase.

components.meaning: art, skill; also a digit of the moon, a portion of power

names.meaning: She who wears the arts as a garland
names.significance: Traditionally the sixty-four arts (catuḥṣaṣṭi kalāḥ) are meant, strung together as Her ornament; kalā can also be read as the digits of the moon or the subtle portions of Her power.

meaning_check.note: 'Sixty-four' is the traditional count, not part of the name; it is moved to the significance.

names.uncertain: Ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('the garland of the arts') and bahuvrīhi ('whose garland is the arts') readings are both current.

samasa.vigraha: कामान् दोग्धि इति कामधुक्
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmān dogdhi iti kāmadhuk
samasa.explanation: The final member dhuk is a root-noun from √duh 'to milk' with the zero suffix kvip, which can stand only at the end of a compound with its object as the upapada: 'one who milks out desires', i.e. yields what is wished for.

components.note: √duh + zero suffix; at the word's end h becomes gh and then k, and the initial d is aspirated to dh because the aspiration of h is lost (nominative duh → dhuk)

names.meaning: She who fulfills all desires
names.significance: The name calls up Kāmadhenu, the wish-yielding cow; as the cow gives milk freely to her calf, She yields to Her devotees whatever they seek, worldly and spiritual.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, made possessive by the suffix -in (alternatively ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: कामेन रूपम् कामरूपम्; कामरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति कामरूपिणी; अथवा कामस्य रूपम् कामरूपम्
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāmena rūpam kāmarūpam; kāmarūpam asyāḥ asti iti kāmarūpiṇī; athavā kāmasya rūpam kāmarūpam
samasa.explanation: (1) kāma-rūpa 'form (taken) at will' — kāma here means 'free choice', the instrumental relation of a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. (2) The possessive suffix -in, feminine -iṇī, makes it 'She who has forms at will', i.e. takes any form She wishes. Read as a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, kāmarūpa is 'the form of Kāma (Kāmeśvara or the god of love)', and the name becomes 'She who has the form of Kāma'.

components.meaning: will, wish; also Kāma (Kāmeśvara, the god of love)

components.note: rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who assumes any form at will
names.significance: Traditionally also read as the presiding Goddess of Kāmarūpa, the Śakti-pīṭha of Kāmākhyā, and as She whose form is one with Kāmeśvara.

meaning_check.note: 'Desirable form' takes kāma as an adjective; the compound means 'form at will' (or 'the form of Kāma').

names.previous_split_issues: kāma was glossed only 'desire/wish'; in this compound it is 'will, free choice' (or the god Kāma).
names.uncertain: Three readings are current: 'taking form at will', 'having the form of Kāma/Kāmeśvara', and 'Goddess of Kāmarūpa'.

samasa.vigraha: कलानाम् निधिः कलानिधिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: kalānām nidhiḥ kalānidhiḥ
samasa.explanation: nidhi 'treasury, store' is the head and kalā stands to it in the genitive: 'the treasury of the arts'. The masculine noun nidhi keeps its own gender as Her name.

names.meaning: She who is the treasure-house of all arts
names.significance: Kalānidhi is also a name of the moon, the 'store of digits'; traditionally She is the moon that holds all sixteen kalās, and the source of every art.

meaning_check.note: 'treasurehouse' respelled.

samasa.vigraha: काव्यम् एव कला काव्यकला; अथवा काव्यस्य कला काव्यकला
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāvyam eva kalā kāvyakalā; athavā kāvyasya kalā kāvyakalā
samasa.explanation: kalā is the head. As a karmadhāraya: 'the art that is poetry'; as a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa: 'the art of poetry'. The sense is the same.

components.meaning: poetry, the work of a poet (kavi)

names.meaning: She who is the art of poetry
names.significance: Traditionally all poetry and song are Her form, and She grants the gift of poetic speech to Her devotees.

samasa.vigraha: रसम् जानाति इति रसज्ञा
samasa.vigraha_iast: rasam jānāti iti rasajñā
samasa.explanation: jña 'knowing' is formed from √jñā with the suffix -a and stands only at the end of a compound, with its object (rasa) as the upapada: 'one who knows rasa'; feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who knows all the rasas
names.significance: Rasa is both the flavor of things and the aesthetic emotion of poetry and drama; She knows every rasa. Rasajñā is also a word for the tongue, the organ that knows taste.

samasa.vigraha: रसस्य शेवधिः रसशेवधिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: rasasya śevadhiḥ rasaśevadhiḥ
samasa.explanation: śevadhi 'treasure' is the head and rasa stands to it in the genitive: 'the treasure of rasa'. The masculine noun keeps its gender as Her name.

names.meaning: She who is the treasure-house of rasa
names.significance: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad says of the Self raso vai saḥ, 'He is rasa; obtaining rasa one becomes blissful'; She is the store of that bliss.

meaning_check.note: 'treasurehouse' respelled.

names.meaning: She who is full of vigor and abundantly nourished
names.significance: Traditionally She is the fullness that nourishes every being; Puṣṭi, 'nourishment', is counted among Her powers.

meaning_check.note: 'always' is not in the name; wording tidied.

components.note: the indeclinable purā 'formerly' + the suffix -tana, feminine

names.meaning: She who is ancient
names.significance: She is the primordial one, existing before all that was created.

components.meaning: to be worshipped, worthy of worship

names.meaning: She who is worthy of worship by all
names.significance: As the gerundive says, worship is Her due; traditionally even the gods worship Her.

components.note: puṣkara 'blue lotus, water, sky; the tīrtha Puṣkara', used as an adjective with feminine -ā; traditionally linked with √puṣ 'to nourish'

names.meaning: She who is whole and gives nourishment to all
names.significance: Traditionally read as She who nourishes all, connecting the name with puṣṭā (801); puṣkara also names the lotus, the sky and the holy lake Puṣkara.

meaning_check.note: Typo 'bourishment' corrected; wording tidied.

names.uncertain: puṣkara has many senses (lotus, water, sky, the tīrtha Puṣkara); the gloss 'nourishing' rests on a traditional etymology from √puṣ rather than on regular grammar.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: पुष्करे इव ईक्षणे यस्याः सा पुष्करेक्षणा
samasa.vigraha_iast: puṣkare iva īkṣaṇe yasyāḥ sā puṣkarekṣaṇā
samasa.explanation: A comparison folded into a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose eyes (īkṣaṇa) are like lotuses (puṣkara)'. īkṣaṇa takes the feminine -ā to agree with Her.

names.meaning: She who has eyes like lotus petals
names.significance: Lotus eyes are the classical sign of grace: wide, cool and compassionate, they rest on the devotee as a lotus opens to the sun.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is puṣkara + īkṣaṇa, joined by guṇa (a + ī → e).

sandhi.rule: a word-final m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which here takes the nasal of the following palatal, ñ (optional, 8.4.59 vā padāntasya)

components.note: neuter nominative singular of para, agreeing with jyotiḥ

names.meaning: She who is the supreme light
names.significance: The Chāndogya Upaniṣad speaks of the self that, 'reaching the supreme light (paraṃ jyotir upasampadya)', appears in its own form; She is that light, by which sun, moon and fire shine.
names.previous_split_issues: 'parañ' was given in its sandhi form; the word is param, the neuter of para agreeing with jyotiḥ, and the name is a two-word phrase rather than a compound.

sandhi.rule: a word-final m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which here takes the nasal of the following dental, n (optional, 8.4.59 vā padāntasya)

components.note: neuter nominative singular of para, agreeing with dhāma

names.meaning: She who is the supreme abode
names.significance: The Bhagavad Gītā (10.12) calls the Lord paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma, 'the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode'; She is the final resting place from which there is no return.
names.previous_split_issues: 'paran' was given in its sandhi form; the word is param, agreeing with the neuter dhāma, and the name is a two-word phrase rather than a compound.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: परमः अणुः परमाणुः
samasa.vigraha_iast: paramaḥ aṇuḥ paramāṇuḥ
samasa.explanation: parama 'utmost' qualifies aṇu 'minute particle', the head: 'the utmost-minute one', the subtlest particle. The masculine aṇu keeps its gender as Her name.

names.meaning: She who is the subtlest particle
names.significance: The Kaṭha Upaniṣad describes the Self as aṇor aṇīyān, 'subtler than the subtle'; She pervades even the smallest thing and is too fine to be grasped by the senses.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is parama + aṇu, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.type: pañcamī-tatpuruṣa of the aluk kind (the first member keeps its ablative ending)
samasa.vigraha: परात् परा परात्परा
samasa.vigraha_iast: parāt parā parātparā
samasa.explanation: parā 'higher, supreme' is the head; parāt 'than the high' is an ablative of comparison and keeps its case ending inside the compound (aluk): 'higher than the highest'. It can equally be taken as a fixed two-word phrase.

names.meaning: She who is the most supreme of the supreme ones
names.significance: Nothing stands beyond Her: She transcends even what is called supreme, such as the deities of creation, preservation and dissolution.

meaning_check.note: Typo 'tshe' corrected.

names.previous_split_issues: parāt was glossed simply 'supreme'; it is the ablative 'than the supreme'.
names.uncertain: Whether parātparā is an aluk compound or a two-word phrase written together is a matter of analysis; the meaning is the same.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (vyadhikaraṇa: the members are in different cases)
samasa.vigraha: पाशः हस्ते यस्याः सा पाशहस्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: pāśaḥ haste yasyāḥ sā pāśahastā
samasa.explanation: 'She in whose hand (hasta) is the noose (pāśa)': the noose is nominative, the hand locative, so the bahuvrīhi joins members that do not agree. hasta takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: hasta with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who holds a noose in Her hand
names.significance: The noose is one of Her four emblems (name 8 describes it as the power of attachment); holding it She binds, and the next name says She also cuts every bond.

samasa.vigraha: पाशानाम् हन्त्री पाशहन्त्री
samasa.vigraha_iast: pāśānām hantrī pāśahantrī
samasa.explanation: hantrī 'destroyer' (agent noun from √han) is the head and the nooses stand to it in the genitive. Pāṇini restricts such compounds of an object with a -tṛ agent noun (2.2.15), but names of this shape are admitted as compounds of general relation (śeṣa-ṣaṣṭhī).

names.meaning: She who destroys the bonds
names.significance: In Śaiva doctrine the soul in bondage is the paśu, held by the pāśa of impurity, karma and māyā; She who holds the noose (810) is also the one who severs it.

samasa.vigraha: परेषाम् मन्त्राः परमन्त्राः; परमन्त्राणाम् विभेदिनी परमन्त्रविभेदिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: pareṣām mantrāḥ paramantrāḥ; paramantrāṇām vibhedinī paramantravibhedinī
samasa.explanation: (1) para-mantra 'the mantras of others', i.e. of enemies (para here is 'other, hostile', not 'supreme'). (2) vibhedinī 'one who breaks apart' is the head, with those mantras in the genitive.

components.meaning: mantra, spell; also counsel, secret plan

components.note: vi + √bhid 'to split' + the agent suffix -in, feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who shatters the mantras employed by enemies
names.significance: Traditionally She protects the devotee from hostile spells and rites; mantra can also mean an enemy's counsel, which She brings to nothing.

meaning_check.note: 'evil' is not in the name; para is simply 'other, hostile'.

names.previous_split_issues: para was glossed 'supreme'; here it means 'other, hostile, enemy'.

components.note: √mūrch 'to congeal, take shape', past participle, feminine

names.meaning: She who has forms
names.significance: The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (2.3.1) says Brahman has two forms, the formed (mūrta) and the formless (amūrta); names 813 and 814 give Her both.

samasa.vigraha: न मूर्ता अमूर्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: na mūrtā amūrtā
samasa.explanation: The negative particle na appears as a- before a consonant and negates the head mūrtā: 'not having form'.

components.note: the negative particle na in composition

names.meaning: She who has no definite form
names.significance: Paired with 813: as the formless She is the unmanifest Brahman beyond the reach of the senses, and the formed and the formless are equally Her.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is the negative a- + mūrtā.

samasa.vigraha: न नित्यम् अनित्यम्; अनित्यैः तृप्ता अनित्यतृप्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: na nityam anityam; anityaiḥ tṛptā anityatṛptā
samasa.explanation: (1) a-nitya 'not lasting, perishable' (nañ-tatpuruṣa). (2) The participle tṛptā 'satisfied' is the head and takes perishable things in the instrumental: 'satisfied with what is perishable'.

names.meaning: She who is satisfied even by our perishable offerings
names.significance: Traditionally read as Her grace: the Eternal is pleased with transient offerings such as a flower, a leaf or water given with devotion.
names.uncertain: The śloka's continuous text mūrtāmūrtānitya… could also be divided amūrtā + nityatṛptā 'ever satisfied'; the edited text marks the a of anitya with an avagraha, following the traditional division.

samasa.vigraha: मुनीनाम् मानसम् मुनिमानसम्; मुनिमानसे हंसिका मुनिमानसहंसिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: munīnām mānasam munimānasam; munimānase haṃsikā munimānasahaṃsikā
samasa.explanation: (1) muni-mānasa 'the mind of sages' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) haṃsikā 'swan' is the head and the mind is its locative: 'the swan in the sages' mind'. mānasa is a double meaning: 'mind' and Lake Mānasa, the swans' home; the sages' mind is that lake.

components.note: haṃsī 'female swan' with the suffix -ka (affectionate); ī shortened before it

names.meaning: She who is the swan in the Mānasa lake that is the minds of sages
names.significance: As swans dwell on Lake Mānasa, She sports in the still minds of sages; the haṃsa is also the breath-mantra haṃsa/so 'ham and the soul's discrimination of the real from the unreal.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'mAnasa' respelled; the lake–mind double meaning made explicit.

samasa.vigraha: सत्यम् व्रतम् यस्याः सा सत्यव्रता
samasa.vigraha_iast: satyam vratam yasyāḥ sā satyavratā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose vow (vrata) is truth (satya)': the two members agree and together describe Her; vrata takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: vrata with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose vow is truth, who abides firmly in truth
names.significance: Traditionally She never departs from Her word, and She is reached by those whose observance is truthfulness.

meaning_check.note: The bahuvrīhi 'whose vow is truth' added to the previous paraphrase.

samasa.vigraha: सत्यम् रूपम् यस्याः सा सत्यरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: satyam rūpam yasyāḥ sā satyarūpā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose form (rūpa) is truth': rūpa takes the feminine -ā; She is truth itself, not a possessor of it.

components.note: rūpa with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is truth itself
names.significance: Traditionally connected with the Upaniṣadic satyasya satyam, 'the truth of truth': She is the reality on which all relative truths rest.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (the final member itself an upapada compound)
samasa.vigraha: अन्तः यच्छति इति अन्तर्यामिनी; सर्वेषाम् अन्तर्यामिनी सर्वान्तर्यामिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: antaḥ yacchati iti antaryāminī; sarveṣām antaryāminī sarvāntaryāminī
samasa.explanation: (1) antar-yāmin 'the one who controls from within' (antar 'within' + √yam 'to restrain, guide' + -in). (2) It is the head of a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa with sarva 'all': 'the inner controller of all'.

names.meaning: She who is the inner ruler dwelling within all
names.significance: The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad's antaryāmin teaching describes the Self that dwells in every being and rules it from within, unknown to it; She is that inner controller.

meaning_check.note: 'Dwells inside' kept, and yāminī 'ruler, controller' added: the antaryāmin both indwells and governs.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is sarva + antar + yāminī (antaryāmin, the Upaniṣadic inner controller).

names.meaning: She who is Being itself, the Real; She who is Satī
names.significance: As sat She is pure existence, the ground of all that is; She is also Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa who gave up her body rather than hear Śiva reviled, and from whose limbs the Śakti-pīṭhas arose.

meaning_check.note: 'eternal' is not in the name; the second traditional sense, Satī, added.

components.note: feminine of brahman / Brahmā, formed like indrāṇī and rudrāṇī; n becomes ṇ after r (ṇatva)

names.meaning: She who is Brahmāṇī, the creative power of Brahmā
names.significance: Brahmāṇī is one of the mother-goddesses (Mātṛkās). Traditionally the name is also connected with the Taittirīya Upaniṣad's brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā, 'Brahman is the tail, the support', which lies behind the older rendering.

meaning_check.note: The older rendering 'the tail that is Brahman' gives only a commentarial interpretation as though it were the translation; the name itself is the feminine of Brahmā/Brahman.

names.uncertain: The traditional interpretation through 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' rests on a derivation that could not be confirmed; the plain grammatical sense is given as the meaning.

sandhi.rule: No sound change: the śloka's ब्रह्मजननी is divided by Bhāskararāya into two names, ब्रह्म (822) and जननी (823). brahma is the neuter nominative singular of brahman (the final n is lost at the end of the word), so the two words simply stand side by side.

components.note: nominative singular of the neuter n-stem brahman

names.meaning: She who is Brahman
names.significance: The Goddess is identified with the Absolute of the Upaniṣads, without attributes and beyond all names; the neuter noun keeps its own gender as Her name.

meaning_check.note: Capitalized Brahman.

names.variants: Read as one word, ब्रह्मजननी would be the single name 'Mother of Brahmā (or of Brahman)', as some popular lists take it; Bhāskararāya's count of a thousand requires two names here.

sandhi.rule: No sound change: jananī is the second of the two names into which Bhāskararāya divides the śloka's ब्रह्मजननी (see 822).

names.meaning: She who is the Mother
names.significance: Standing on its own, the name makes Her the mother of all without limit; read with 822, the Absolute itself is the one who gives birth.

meaning_check.note: Capitalized Mother.

names.variants: See 822: some lists read ब्रह्मजननी as one name.

samasa.vigraha: बहूनि रूपाणि यस्याः सा बहुरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: bahūni rūpāṇi yasyāḥ sā bahurūpā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose forms are many': bahu 'many' and rūpa 'form' agree and together describe Her; rūpa takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: rūpa with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who has a multitude of forms
names.significance: The Kaṭha Upaniṣad speaks of the one who 'makes the one form manifold' (ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti); every form in the universe is Hers.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: बुधैः अर्चिता बुधार्चिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: budhaiḥ arcitā budhārcitā
samasa.explanation: The participle arcitā 'worshipped' is the head and the wise are the agents in the instrumental: 'worshipped by the wise'.

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by the wise
names.significance: Traditionally the wise are those who know Her true nature; budha can also be the planet Mercury or the gods, all of whom worship Her.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is budha + arcitā, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

components.note: pra + √sū 'to beget, set in motion' + the agent suffix -tṛ (with i), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is mother of the universe
names.significance: Traditionally the name is connected with Savitṛ, the impeller of the Gāyatrī mantra: She is the one who brings the whole universe forth.

samasa.vigraha: प्रकर्षेण चण्डा प्रचण्डा
samasa.vigraha_iast: prakarṣeṇa caṇḍā pracaṇḍā
samasa.explanation: The prefix pra 'forth, exceedingly' intensifies the head caṇḍā 'fierce': 'exceedingly fierce'.

names.meaning: She who is full of awe-inspiring wrath
names.significance: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad says that from fear of the Absolute the wind blows and the sun rises; Her fierceness is that awe which keeps the cosmic order, and it is turned against the devotee's foes.

names.meaning: She who is the divine command Herself
names.significance: Her command is the law of the universe, which even the gods obey; ājñā is also the cakra between the eyebrows, the 'command' center, where She is meditated upon.

meaning_check.note: Capitalized Herself; wording tidied.

sandhi.rule: after the i of the prefix prati the s of sthā becomes ṣ (Pāṇini 8.3.65), and th then becomes ṭh next to ṣ (ṣṭutva, Pāṇini 8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ)

components.note: √sthā; prati + √sthā gives the feminine noun pratiṣṭhā 'standing firm, foundation'

names.meaning: She who is the foundation
names.significance: She is the ground on which everything stands (the Taittirīya Upaniṣad's brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā). Pratiṣṭhā is also the second of the five kalās of Śaiva doctrine, which name 853 brings to its summit.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: प्रकटा आकृतिः यस्याः सा प्रकटाकृतिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: prakaṭā ākṛtiḥ yasyāḥ sā prakaṭākṛtiḥ
samasa.explanation: 'She whose form (ākṛti) is manifest (prakaṭā)'. The feminine adjective prakaṭā takes its masculine stem prakaṭa in the compound (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.34). The final member ākṛti is already feminine and keeps its nominative -iḥ.

names.meaning: She whose form is manifest
names.significance: Traditionally She is manifest to everyone as the sense 'I am'. In Śrīvidyā the yoginīs of the outermost enclosure of the Śrīcakra are called prakaṭa 'manifest', and the name is also read as Her having them for Her form.

meaning_check.note: 'In the form of the universe' is not in the name; the bahuvrīhi says only that Her form is manifest.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is prakaṭa + ākṛti, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: प्राणानाम् ईश्वरी प्राणेश्वरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: prāṇānām īśvarī prāṇeśvarī
samasa.explanation: īśvarī 'ruler' is the head and the prāṇas stand to it in the genitive: 'the ruler of the vital breaths'. In the Upaniṣads prāṇāḥ (plural) also means the senses.

components.meaning: vital breath; in the plural, the senses

names.meaning: She who rules over the prāṇas and the senses
names.significance: Traditionally also 'Queen of life' in the sense of beloved: She is the life-breath of Śiva, and of every living being.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'prANas' respelled; 'the five' is not in the name.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is prāṇa + īśvarī, joined by guṇa.

samasa.vigraha: प्राणानाम् दात्री प्राणदात्री
samasa.vigraha_iast: prāṇānām dātrī prāṇadātrī
samasa.explanation: dātrī 'giver' (agent noun from √dā) is the head and the prāṇas stand to it in the genitive: 'the giver of life-breath' (on such compounds with -tṛ see name 811).

names.meaning: She who is the giver of life
names.significance: She gives breath to every creature; the Kauṣītaki and other Upaniṣads identify prāṇa with consciousness, so She gives both life and awareness.

samasa.type: dvigu (numeral karmadhāraya), made possessive by the suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: पञ्चाशत् पीठानि पञ्चाशत्पीठानि; पञ्चाशत्पीठानि रूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: pañcāśat pīṭhāni pañcāśatpīṭhāni; pañcāśatpīṭhāni rūpam asyāḥ asti iti pañcāśatpīṭharūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) pañcāśat-pīṭha 'the fifty seats': a numeral qualifying a noun, i.e. a dvigu, allowed because a further member follows. (2) That compound with rūpa 'form' takes the possessive suffix -in (feminine -iṇī): 'She whose form is the fifty seats'. The final t of pañcāśat is unchanged before p.

components.meaning: seat; a sacred seat of the Goddess

components.note: rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She whose form is the fifty sacred seats (pīṭhas)
names.significance: Traditionally the fifty pīṭhas correspond to the fifty letters of the Sanskrit alphabet (the mātṛkās), placed on the body in nyāsa; the sacred places of the land and the sounds of speech are both Her body.

meaning_check.note: 'Has fifty centers' made precise: the rūpiṇī says the pīṭhas are Her form.

samasa.vigraha: विगतानि शृङ्खलानि यस्याः सा विशृङ्खला
samasa.vigraha_iast: vigatāni śṛṅkhalāni yasyāḥ sā viśṛṅkhalā
samasa.explanation: The prefix vi stands for vigata 'gone': 'She from whom fetters (śṛṅkhala) are gone', i.e. who is bound by nothing. The final member takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: śṛṅkhala, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is unfettered, free in every way
names.significance: Traditionally She is bound by no rule, karma or injunction, being the source of all laws; She also frees Her devotees from every chain.

samasa.vigraha: विविक्ते तिष्ठति इति विविक्तस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: vivikte tiṣṭhati iti viviktasthā
samasa.explanation: stha 'standing, dwelling' is formed from √sthā with the suffix -a after a word in the locative (Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ): 'one who dwells in a secluded place'; feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who abides in secluded places
names.significance: Traditionally She dwells in solitary, pure places and in the discerning mind (viveka) of those who sift the real from the unreal.

samasa.vigraha: वीराणाम् माता वीरमाता
samasa.vigraha_iast: vīrāṇām mātā vīramātā
samasa.explanation: mātā 'mother' is the head and the heroes stand to it in the genitive.

components.note: nominative singular of the stem mātṛ

names.meaning: She who is the mother of the valiant
names.significance: In Tantra the vīra is the adept of the heroic disposition (vīrabhāva); She is mother to the courageous in battle and in sādhana.

samasa.vigraha: वियतः प्रसूः वियत्प्रसूः
samasa.vigraha_iast: viyataḥ prasūḥ viyatprasūḥ
samasa.explanation: prasū 'mother, one who brings forth' is the head and the sky stands to it in the genitive: 'mother of space'. prasū is a root-noun (pra + √sū), so its nominative ends in -ūḥ.

names.meaning: She who is the mother of the ether (space)
names.significance: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad says that from the Self space (ākāśa) first arose; She is the source of space, the first of the elements, and so of all the rest.

meaning_check.note: 'mother to the ether' tidied.

components.note: feminine of Mukunda, a name of Viṣṇu; traditionally explained as muku 'liberation' + √dā 'to give'

names.meaning: She who grants liberation; She who is Mukundā, one with Viṣṇu
names.significance: Mukunda is Viṣṇu, and She is His feminine counterpart (the Goddess as Viṣṇu's own power); the traditional etymology 'giver of muku, liberation' gives the older rendering.

meaning_check.note: 'salvation' replaced by 'liberation', and the plain sense, the feminine of Mukunda (Viṣṇu), added.

names.uncertain: The derivation muku 'liberation' + dā 'giving' is a traditional etymology (nirukti), not regular grammar.

samasa.vigraha: मुक्तेः निलयः मुक्तिनिलयः; मुक्तिनिलयः अस्याः अस्ति इति मुक्तिनिलया; अथवा मुक्तिः निलयः यस्याः सा मुक्तिनिलया
samasa.vigraha_iast: mukteḥ nilayaḥ muktinilayaḥ; muktinilayaḥ asyāḥ asti iti muktinilayā; athavā muktiḥ nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā muktinilayā
samasa.explanation: (1) mukti-nilaya 'the dwelling-place of liberation' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, nilaya the head). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X'). As a bahuvrīhi it reads 'She whose dwelling is liberation'. Either way She and liberation are found in one place.

components.note: ni + √lī 'to rest in'; nilaya with the feminine -ā

names.meaning: She who is the abode of liberation
names.significance: Traditionally the four kinds of liberation (sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya, sāyujya) reside in Her, and She is reached in the state of liberation itself.

meaning_check.note: 'salvation' replaced by 'liberation'.

names.uncertain: The feminine ending admits two analyses: an adjectival ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('the abode of liberation') and a bahuvrīhi ('whose abode is liberation').

samasa.type: karmadhāraya, made possessive by the suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: मूलम् विग्रहः मूलविग्रहः; मूलविग्रहः रूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति मूलविग्रहरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: mūlam vigrahaḥ mūlavigrahaḥ; mūlavigrahaḥ rūpam asyāḥ asti iti mūlavigraharūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) mūla-vigraha 'the root form' (karmadhāraya: mūla 'root, original' qualifies vigraha 'form, embodiment'). (2) With rūpa and the possessive suffix -in: 'She whose form is the root form'.

components.note: rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is the root form of everything
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā She is the original form from which the other forms of the Goddess, such as Bālā and the attendant powers of the Śrīcakra, issue; mūla also recalls the mūlādhāra and the root mantra (mūla-mantra).

samasa.vigraha: भावम् जानाति इति भावज्ञा
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhāvam jānāti iti bhāvajñā
samasa.explanation: jña 'knowing' (√jñā + -a) stands at the end of the compound with its object bhāva as the upapada: 'one who knows (inner) states'; feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who is the knower of all thoughts and sentiments
names.significance: She knows the intention behind every act of devotion, and so accepts even an imperfect offering made with a true heart; bhāva also means existence, all of which She knows.

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya of identification)
samasa.vigraha: भवः एव रोगः भवरोगः; भवरोगम् हन्ति इति भवरोगघ्नी
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhavaḥ eva rogaḥ bhavarogaḥ; bhavarogam hanti iti bhavarogaghnī
samasa.explanation: (1) bhava-roga 'the disease that is worldly existence': a karmadhāraya of identification (rūpaka) — existence itself is the disease. (2) ghnī 'destroying' (from √han) stands at the end with the disease as its object (upapada-tatpuruṣa).

components.meaning: worldly existence, the round of birth and death

components.note: √han 'to strike' + -a; the root vowel drops and h becomes gh before n; feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who destroys the disease of worldly existence, the round of birth and death
names.significance: Traditionally saṃsāra is the disease and knowledge of Her the remedy; She is the physician of the soul.

meaning_check.note: The compound is a rūpaka: existence is itself the disease, not a source of 'diseases'.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya of identification)
samasa.vigraha: भवः एव चक्रम् भवचक्रम्; भवचक्रस्य प्रवर्तिनी भवचक्रप्रवर्तिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhavaḥ eva cakram bhavacakram; bhavacakrasya pravartinī bhavacakrapravartinī
samasa.explanation: (1) bhava-cakra 'the wheel that is worldly existence' (rūpaka karmadhāraya). (2) pravartinī 'she who sets in motion' is the head, with the wheel in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who turns the wheel of the cycle of birth and death
names.significance: The same Power that frees (842) also keeps the wheel of existence turning, by Her will, for the ripening of every soul's karma.

sandhi.rule: the final s of chandas becomes visarga at the end of a member and, before s, may stay as visarga instead of s (optional, Pāṇini 8.3.36 vā śari)

samasa.vigraha: छन्दसाम् सारः छन्दःसारः; छन्दःसारः अस्याः अस्ति इति छन्दःसारा
samasa.vigraha_iast: chandasām sāraḥ chandaḥsāraḥ; chandaḥsāraḥ asyāḥ asti iti chandaḥsārā
samasa.explanation: (1) chandaḥ-sāra 'the essence of the Vedas' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, sāra the head). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X').

names.meaning: She who is the essence of the Vedas
names.significance: Chandas is the Veda as metrical hymn; traditionally the Gāyatrī, the 'mother of the Vedas', is their essence and is Her form.

meaning_check.note: 'all the vedas' tidied; chandas (the Vedas as hymns) is kept in view.

names.previous_split_issues: chandaḥ was given in its sandhi form; the stem is chandas.

samasa.vigraha: शास्त्राणाम् सारः शास्त्रसारः; शास्त्रसारः अस्याः अस्ति इति शास्त्रसारा
samasa.vigraha_iast: śāstrāṇām sāraḥ śāstrasāraḥ; śāstrasāraḥ asyāḥ asti iti śāstrasārā
samasa.explanation: (1) śāstra-sāra 'the essence of the scriptures' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X').

names.meaning: She who is the essence of all scriptures
names.significance: Every śāstra, from the Vedas and Upaniṣads to the Tantras and Purāṇas, has Her as its final import.

samasa.vigraha: मन्त्राणाम् सारः मन्त्रसारः; मन्त्रसारः अस्याः अस्ति इति मन्त्रसारा
samasa.vigraha_iast: mantrāṇām sāraḥ mantrasāraḥ; mantrasāraḥ asyāḥ asti iti mantrasārā
samasa.explanation: (1) mantra-sāra 'the essence of mantras' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X').

names.meaning: She who is the essence of all mantras
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā the fifteen-syllabled Pañcadaśī (and its sixteen-syllabled form) is regarded as the crown of all mantras, and it is Her very form.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: तलम् इव उदरम् यस्याः सा तलोदरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: talam iva udaram yasyāḥ sā talodarī
samasa.explanation: 'She whose belly (udara) is like a flat surface (tala)', i.e. slender-waisted. A bahuvrīhi ending in a word for a body part may take the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54).

components.meaning: flat surface, palm; also the nether worlds (atala, vitala …)

components.note: udara with the feminine -ī of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is slender-waisted
names.significance: The slender waist is a classical mark of beauty; traditionally the name is also read as She in whose belly lie the lower worlds (talas), the cosmic form containing all regions.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is tala + udara, joined by guṇa (a + u → o).
names.uncertain: Two readings are current: 'whose waist is flat (slender)' and 'in whose belly are the talas, the lower worlds'.

samasa.vigraha: उदारा कीर्तिः यस्याः सा उदारकीर्तिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: udārā kīrtiḥ yasyāḥ sā udārakīrtiḥ
samasa.explanation: 'She whose fame (kīrti) is exalted (udārā)'. The feminine adjective takes its masculine stem udāra in the compound (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.34); kīrti is already feminine and keeps its nominative -iḥ.

names.meaning: She who possesses exalted fame
names.significance: Her glory is sung everywhere and Her fame is generous: it is sung by those whom She has blessed.

samasa.vigraha: उद्गतम् दाम यस्मात् तत् उद्दाम; उद्दाम वैभवम् यस्याः सा उद्दामवैभवा
samasa.vigraha_iast: udgatam dāma yasmāt tat uddāma; uddāma vaibhavam yasyāḥ sā uddāmavaibhavā
samasa.explanation: (1) ud-dāman 'from which the rope has gone', i.e. unbound, unrestrained (prādi-bahuvrīhi; ud stands for udgata). (2) 'She whose might (vaibhava) is unbounded' (bahuvrīhi); vaibhava takes the feminine -ā. The d of ud meets the d of dāma without change.

components.note: vaibhava (from vibhu 'pervading, mighty'), with the feminine -ā

names.meaning: She whose prowess is unlimited
names.significance: Her power is bound by nothing; the whole creation is only a fraction of Her glory.
names.previous_split_issues: uddāma was left unanalysed; it is ud + dāman 'unbound'.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya of identification, made possessive by the suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: वर्णाः एव रूपम् वर्णरूपम्; वर्णरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति वर्णरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: varṇāḥ eva rūpam varṇarūpam; varṇarūpam asyāḥ asti iti varṇarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) varṇa-rūpa 'the form that is the letters' (karmadhāraya of identification). (2) The possessive suffix -in (feminine -iṇī) makes it 'She whose form is the letters'.

components.meaning: letter, sound of the alphabet; also color, class

components.note: rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

names.meaning: She whose form is the letters of the alphabet
names.significance: The fifty letters (mātṛkā), from a to kṣa, are traditionally Her body; all speech and all mantras are woven from them.

meaning_check.note: 'alphabets' corrected to 'alphabet'; wording follows the rūpiṇī.

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over a dvandva, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, a karmadhāraya and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: जन्म च मृत्युः च जरा च जन्ममृत्युजराः; जन्ममृत्युजराभिः तप्ताः जन्ममृत्युजरातप्ताः; जन्ममृत्युजरातप्ताः जनाः जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनाः; जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनानाम् विश्रान्तिः जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिः; ताम् ददाति इति जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिदायिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: janma ca mṛtyuḥ ca jarā ca janmamṛtyujarāḥ; janmamṛtyujarābhiḥ taptāḥ janmamṛtyujarātaptāḥ; janmamṛtyujarātaptāḥ janāḥ janmamṛtyujarātaptajanāḥ; janmamṛtyujarātaptajanānām viśrāntiḥ janmamṛtyujarātaptajanaviśrāntiḥ; tām dadāti iti janmamṛtyujarātaptajanaviśrāntidāyinī
samasa.explanation: (1) janma-mṛtyu-jarā 'birth, death and old age' (dvandva). (2) …-tapta 'scorched by them' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) …tapta-jana 'people so scorched' (karmadhāraya). (4) …jana-viśrānti 'their rest' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) dāyinī 'giver' is the head, with the rest as its object (upapada-tatpuruṣa). janman appears as janma- in composition (loss of final n).

components.note: appears as janma- in the compound

names.meaning: She who gives peace and repose to those who are afflicted by birth, death and decrepitude
names.significance: Birth, death and old age are the threefold heat of saṃsāra; traditionally She is the shade in which the scorched traveler rests, the final repose of liberation.
names.previous_split_issues: janma was given in its compound form; the stem is janman.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सर्वाः उपनिषदः सर्वोपनिषदः; सर्वोपनिषद्भिः उद्घुष्टा सर्वोपनिषदुद्घुष्टा
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarvāḥ upaniṣadaḥ sarvopaniṣadaḥ; sarvopaniṣadbhiḥ udghuṣṭā sarvopaniṣadudghuṣṭā
samasa.explanation: (1) sarva-upaniṣad 'all the Upaniṣads' (karmadhāraya; sarva is the qualifier). (2) The participle udghuṣṭā 'proclaimed aloud' is the head and the Upaniṣads are its agents in the instrumental. The stem-final d of upaniṣad simply stands before the vowel u.

names.meaning: She who is proclaimed by all the Upaniṣads
names.significance: All the Upaniṣads declare the one Brahman, and in Śrīvidyā that Brahman is the Goddess; their teaching proclaims Her.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'upaniShads' respelled; udghuṣṭā is 'proclaimed aloud' rather than 'celebrated'.

names.previous_split_issues: sarvopaniṣad was left fused (sarva + upaniṣad, guṇa).

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)
savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and a dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: शान्तिम् अतीता शान्त्यतीता; शान्त्यतीता कला शान्त्यतीतकला; शान्त्यतीतकला आत्मा यस्याः सा शान्त्यतीतकलात्मिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: śāntim atītā śāntyatītā; śāntyatītā kalā śāntyatītakalā; śāntyatītakalā ātmā yasyāḥ sā śāntyatītakalātmikā
samasa.explanation: (1) śānti-atītā 'gone beyond śānti' (dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa with atīta, Pāṇini 2.1.24). (2) It qualifies kalā (karmadhāraya); the feminine first member takes its masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with ātman 'self, nature', which in this position appears as -ātmaka, feminine -ātmikā: 'She whose very nature is the kalā beyond śānti'.

components.meaning: kalā, a phase or power of manifestation

names.meaning: She whose very nature is the kalā beyond peace (śāntyatītā)
names.significance: In Śaiva and Śākta doctrine the five kalās (nivṛtti, pratiṣṭhā, vidyā, śānti, śāntyatītā) are the phases through which consciousness descends into the world; the fifth, beyond peace, is the subtlest, and it is Her nature.

meaning_check.note: The name does not say She transcends peace in general: it names the fifth kalā, śāntyatītā, as Her nature.

names.previous_split_issues: śāntyatīta was glossed 'turīyātīta', a different term; neither member was split (śānti + atīta, kalā + ātmikā).

names.meaning: She who is unfathomable
names.significance: Like a deep lake whose bottom cannot be seen, She cannot be measured by the mind or by speech.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: गगनस्य अन्तः गगनान्तः; गगनान्ते तिष्ठति इति गगनान्तस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: gaganasya antaḥ gaganāntaḥ; gaganānte tiṣṭhati iti gaganāntasthā
samasa.explanation: (1) gagana-anta 'the end (or interior) of the sky' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) stha 'dwelling' (√sthā + -a after a locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) is the head: 'one who dwells there'; feminine -ā. anta can mean both 'limit' and 'inside'.

names.meaning: She who dwells at the farthest bound of space, and within it
names.significance: Traditionally the space meant is also the small space (dahara ākāśa) within the heart, of which the Chāndogya Upaniṣad speaks; She dwells there as pure consciousness.

meaning_check.note: anta 'end, interior' was not rendered; 'resides in the ether' made precise.

names.previous_split_issues: gaganānta was left as one row; it is gagana + anta.
names.uncertain: anta can be read as 'limit' (beyond the sky) or 'interior' (within space); both readings are current.

components.meaning: proud, in whom pride has arisen

names.meaning: She who is proud
names.significance: Traditionally Her pride is the full self-awareness of the sole sovereign of all, who has no equal; it is not the vanity of the limited ego.

samasa.vigraha: गाने लोलुपा गानलोलुपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: gāne lolupā gānalolupā
samasa.explanation: lolupā 'eager, longing' is the head and music is the object of its longing, in the locative.

names.meaning: She who delights in music
names.significance: Traditionally She is pleased by music offered in devotion; nāda, sound itself, is Her form.

samasa.vigraha: कल्पनया रहिता कल्पनारहिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: kalpanayā rahitā kalpanārahitā
samasa.explanation: The participle rahitā 'free from, devoid of' is the head and takes kalpanā in the instrumental.

names.meaning: She who is free from imaginary attributes
names.significance: Traditionally kalpanā is the superimposition by which the mind imagines name, form and distinction on the Real; She is free of it, being pure consciousness.

components.meaning: limit, goal; direction; a unit of time

names.meaning: She who is the highest goal, beyond which there is nothing
names.significance: The Kaṭha Upaniṣad says of the Puruṣa, 'beyond Him there is nothing; He is the limit (kāṣṭhā), He the highest goal'. Kāṣṭhā is also a direction and a small unit of time, all of which are Her.

meaning_check.note: 'Dwells in' is not in the name: She is the limit itself.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: अकम् अन्तयति इति अकान्ता
samasa.vigraha_iast: akam antayati iti akāntā
samasa.explanation: aka 'pain, sin' is the object and antā 'one who brings to an end' (from anta 'end') is the head: 'She who ends sorrow and sin'.

names.meaning: She who ends all sins and sorrows
names.significance: Traditionally read as She who puts an end to the pain and sin of those who turn to Her.
names.uncertain: aka 'pain, sin' is a rare word and the analysis aka + antā is the traditional one; the śloka's sandhi kāṣṭhā'kāntā fixes the initial a, so a reading kāntā 'beloved' is not available here.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: कान्तस्य अर्धम् कान्तार्धम्; कान्तार्धम् विग्रहः यस्याः सा कान्तार्धविग्रहा
samasa.vigraha_iast: kāntasya ardham kāntārdham; kāntārdham vigrahaḥ yasyāḥ sā kāntārdhavigrahā
samasa.explanation: (1) kānta-ardha 'half of the beloved' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose body (vigraha) is half of the Beloved'; vigraha takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: vigraha with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is half the body of Her husband
names.significance: The name evokes Ardhanārīśvara, the Lord who is half woman: Śiva and Śakti share one body, as consciousness and its power are one.
names.previous_split_issues: kāntārdha was left as one row; it is kānta + ardha.

verse_notes.note: Name 791 gives the Vedāntic definition sat-cit-ānanda; 792 sāmarasya is the technical term for the 'one flavor' of Śiva and Śakti.
Names 801–805 all begin with pu-/pū-; 804 puṣkarā and 805 puṣkarekṣaṇā are separate names.
Names 806 and 807 are two-word phrases (param jyotiḥ, param dhāma) whose m has become ñ and n before the next consonant; they are not compounds of para.

external_sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name
savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name

verse_notes.note: Three names hide in mūrtā'mūrtā'nityatṛptā: 813 mūrtā, 814 amūrtā, 815 anityatṛptā. Without the avagrahas the last could be misread as nityatṛptā.

external_sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the double avagraha (ऽऽ) marks the absorbed long ā of ājñā

verse_notes.note: ब्रह्मजननी is two names in Bhāskararāya's count, 822 brahma and 823 jananī, though it is often read as one ('Mother of Brahmā'); pracaṇḍā''jñā is 827 pracaṇḍā + 828 ājñā.
Names 842–843 face each other: She destroys the disease of existence and also turns its wheel.

external_sandhi.rule: visarga after a vowel other than a or ā becomes r before a voiced sound, here the vowel u

verse_notes.note: Divide udārakīrtir uddāmavaibhavā (848, 849): the r belongs to the visarga of kīrtiḥ, not to the next name (not udārakīrti ruddāma).
Name 851 fills the whole first half. Name 853 names the fifth of the five kalās (nivṛtti, pratiṣṭhā, vidyā, śānti, śāntyatītā); pratiṣṭhā (829) is the second.

external_sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name

verse_notes.note: kāṣṭhā'kāntā is 859 kāṣṭhā + 860 akāntā; the avagraha shows that the second name begins with a.

report.summary: Checked all 71 names of ślokas 151–160 against text.json, with sandhi at every member junction, a layered samāsa analysis and the meanings tested against it. Bhāskararāya's division of ब्रह्मजननी into 822 brahma and 823 jananī is kept and explained; 806 and 807 are two-word phrases (param jyotiḥ, param dhāma), not compounds. Meanings were replaced where a commentarial gloss or a wrong sense stood in for the name (792 sāmarasya, 796 kāmarūpiṇī, 821 brahmāṇī, 830 prakaṭākṛtiḥ, 853 śāntyatītā kalā); several old splits glossed para as 'supreme' where it means 'enemy' (812) or gave sandhi forms as stems. No problem was found in the Sanskrit text.
